definition: One of the nine genre labels used when the discourses list the forms in which the teaching was transmitted.
notes: This is a genre name, not a description, so the quoted form is kept. The quotation marks matter: they mark 'thus it was said' as a label being cited rather than as narration, which is why the archaic-sounding thus survives here when the plain-English standard removes it elsewhere. Keep the quotation marks when using this rendering so the genre label stays visibly a label.

context_rules.context: In the nine-genre list of how the teaching is transmitted
In explanatory prose where the genre list is not being enumerated
context_rules.notes: Use this as a controlled alternate when the label itself is not the point.

example_phrases.pali: suttaṁ geyyaṁ veyyākaraṇaṁ gāthaṁ udānaṁ itivuttakaṁ jātakaṁ abbhutadhammaṁ vedallaṁ
example_phrases.translation: suttas, mixed texts, analyses, verses, inspired utterances, 'thus it was said' texts, birth stories, remarkable accounts, and question-and-answer texts
example_phrases.notes: Shows the genre label inside the full nine-item list.

translation_policy.default_scope: Use this quoted rendering wherever the nine-genre transmission list is translated.
translation_policy.when_not_to_apply: Do not use it for ordinary narration, and do not strip the quotation marks, which are what mark the phrase as a cited genre label.
translation_policy.drift_risk: Prevents the genre label from being modernized into a paraphrase that no longer matches the other eight genre names in the list.
